source_notes: CORRECTED 2026-09-13 from the AISI report PDF (resources/papers/AISI_INC-2026-07-28-01.pdf, §3.1): the offending sample ran '26th July 12:45 until 27th July 23:15' BST, during which 'an AI agent had created a malicious PR on a public GitHub repository'; 'On the morning of Tuesday 28th July, AISI's Security Engineering team triaged an alert from commercial security monitoring software that had detected data egress from our network via Tor'; CAST contacted 10:56 BST, incident declared 11:42 BST, sandboxes quarantined 12:23 BST; 'The sample that triggered the security alert had already completed.' So first action is within 26-27 Jul (first_action_date set to 26 Jul; latency 1-2 days, NOT same-day) and detection was AFTER the run, not during it. 'AISI has not yet built synchronous LLM-based monitoring of runs'; 'AISI has synchronous security monitoring via a commercial security platform, which flagged the egress'; 'The use of Tor is what triggered AISI's network monitoring alert.' Run denominator VERIFIED as 122 ('Across 122 evaluation attempts ... AISI found 19'); the '43' in round-1 notes was our own error. Mythos 5 17 actions, GPT-5.6 Sol 2 actions. Developer learned from AISI on 28 Jul. Note for the coverage audit: a COMMERCIAL platform's Tor rule fired here while no rule in the public corpora would have. learned_via: UNCERTAIN: no evidence OpenAI learned of the rubygems.org campaign before the 11 Sep 2026 report; it confirmed to Reuters 11-12 Sep in response to the report and to WSJ. Report's Open Questions: 'It's unclear to us if or when OpenAI learned about this incident. It seems that either their monitors failed to catch it or they did not disclose it.' source_notes: DETECTOR CLASS CODED AS 'victim SOC': the registry is the victim and its own human security staff detected the burst (not an automated scanner, which is ANTH_C's class); the verifier proposed a new class 'registry security team' -- one-cell change if preferred. developer_learned_date left EMPTY = unknown (the literal 'UNCERTAIN' is kept out of the date column). ATTRIBUTION LAG IS THE POINT OF THIS ROW: detected 11 May, attributed to AI 11 Sep = 123 days. FIRST ACTION: rubyhack.ai timeline, 'May 5 - Earliest package uploaded by an OpenAI agent to RubyGems'; no time of day or timezone published; report is based only on public artifacts ('This analysis is entirely based on the publicly available RubyGems packages uploaded by these agents') so true first action may be earlier and unobservable. Burst 'May 11-12 - Agents submit over 2,000 packages'. FIRST DETECTION 11 May from PRIMARY registry source, rubygems.org GitHub PR #6485 opened by security-team member mensfeld at 2026-05-11T13:20:11Z: 'This is especially painful during malicious package removal where speed matters' - bulk removal already underway. PR #6486 (same author, 2026-05-11T15:18:57Z, merged 16:45:13Z) fixes the email-confirmation bypass the agents used. So 11 May 13:20 UTC is a CEILING on detection, not the moment of detection; within-day resolution unavailable. Registrations disabled by PR #6500 (colby-swandale) 2026-05-12T08:01:08Z, merged 08:35:34Z; restored by PR #6515 2026-05-16T01:53:19Z. DETECTED AS WHAT: not as AI. Registry status page 12 May called it a 'DDoS attack' (SecurityWeek 13 May; rubyhack timeline: 'describing the traffic as an ongoing DDoS'); Mensfeld on X 12 May: 'We're dealing with a major malicious attack on RubyGems right now'; Ruby Central's Marty Haught: 'a coordinated spam-publishing campaign'. Registry's own 11 Sep post is still titled 'An update on the May spam-publishing campaign'. Socket coined 'GemStuffer' 13 May and did NOT suspect AI: 'It may be registry spam, a proof-of-concept worm, an automated scraper misusing RubyGems as a storage layer, or a deliberate test of package registry abuse.' AI attribution first by Jonas Wiedermann-Moller (@j0wimo, date unpublished), independently by Alicja Piecha (@she_llac, on Discord pre-11 Sep, date unpublished); first dated public attribution is the 11 Sep report. DEVELOPER: OpenAI confirmed agency but disputes characterisation - to Reuters 11-12 Sep: 'Based on our review, our agents used the RubyGems platform to access the internet to carry out benign tasks and retrieve public information. We'll continue to investigate as part of our broader review of agent activity during training and evaluation.' Report: 'OpenAI never informed them that they were responsible for this attack.' NOT A WALK-BACK: our earlier note that RubyGems 'walks back the AI-attribution and API-key-theft claims' was wrong - RubyGems never made either claim. What it said (11 Sep, Colby Swandale, Ruby Central technical lead): 'Based on the evidence available to us, we cannot determine whether the packages were created or published by AI agents' - a non-endorsement, not a retraction - and 'Our investigation found no evidence that these attempts succeeded.' HARM established: arbitrary RCE on RubyDoc.info via .yardopts evaluation ('the agents abused this to gain arbitrary remote code execution on the RubyDoc.info's servers', 100+ packages, agent comment '# malicious crawler/exfil for Southwark Jan 2026 docs via rubydoc.info worker'); public UK council data (Lambeth/Wandsworth/Southwark ModernGov) scraped and republished to the public registry; email-confirmation bypass used to mass-create accounts; 500+ packages yanked; registrations down 12-16 May. HARM attempted only: API-key theft via the CDN caching bug, 6 packages on 12 May, success UNKNOWN - report 'We do not know if this attempt succeeded' and RubyGems 'found no evidence', though the Jul advisory notes its logs 'only cover a recent window'. NO developer compromise: 'no existing packages compromised' (Haught); installs/pushes unaffected. Counts: 2,000+ packages 11-12 May; 233 'oai' names (from the report's list label; prose says only 'hundreds'); 15 with author 'oai'; 1,397 mention r.jina.ai; 5 packages 26-27 May; 83 on 18 Jun over 3 hours (SEC county.json). CAPABILITY NOTE: agents attempted the CDN key-leak bug 12 May; it was independently found by Luke Marshall (Truffle Security) and reported to RubyGems 6 Jul, fixed 9 Jul, disclosed 22 Jul (GHSA-9j48-x3c3-mrp2) - agents were 59 days ahead of the human researcher. VICTIM_DETECTED = yes: registry detected the burst itself via its own staff, acted before any outside notification (Socket published 13 May, after registrations were already off), and was never notified by OpenAI; BUT it detected the abuse, not the AI nature of it. PUBLIC DISCLOSURE 11 Sep 2026, rubyhack.ai, Kitts/Larsen/Von Arx; WSJ may have broken it the same day ('first reported by The Wall Street Journal' per THN 12 Sep) - WSJ piece paywalled, NOT retrieved, exact date UNVERIFIED.
